detail.body:
## Overview

Add a native Triton per-token FP8 scaled-MM linear backend, with tuned configurations for Radeon AI PRO R9700 / gfx1201. Select it with `--linear-backend triton` for dynamic per-token activation scales and per-channel weight scales.

Related: [#60672](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60672), which enables the existing AITER per-token FP8 backend. This PR provides the vLLM-native implementation and keeps its tuning configurations in vLLM.
this fixes the regression in #57838 without disabling the working but slower `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` in #57861

## Claims

The per-token FP8 runtime lives in `linear/scaled_mm/triton.py` and supports BF16/FP16 output, bias, compiled dynamic shapes, and graph replay. It uses tuned configurations when available and a hardware-aware untuned heuristic on FP8-capable RDNA. The heuristic selects shared, contiguous, split-K, or persistent launches using shape, processor count, and last-level data-cache capacity; unsupported operands retain the shared fallback. The per-token backend is registered only for ROCm and requires `current_platform.supports_fp8()`.

## Validation

### Public benchmark refresh (`b0d2a7cbcd3f3332df8fe7c0b03f6ca726e27abf`)

Refreshed the R9700 BF16 tables using the [public benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b0d2a7cbcd3f3332df8fe7c0b03f6ca726e27abf/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py) for Gemma 4 12B TP1/TP2: 192 searches across powers-of-two M=1 through 32768, completed in 27.19 minutes. The script now uses the shared GEMM shape catalog with independent model TP and tuning GPU selection; it does not infer attention heads or load model configuration/weights.

The final 11 tables contain **111 tuned entries / 65 heuristic fallbacks**, with **77 entries changed** from `dba246dd44`. Independent hot/rotating runtime validation retained 12 previous choices and applied one further heuristic fallback to the raw search output. Tuning candidates and final validated tables are distinct; fresh timings can select different winners.

| Warmed graph GPU time (geometric mean) | vs previous tables | vs heuristic-only | vs Torch RowWise |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Hot operands, 176 cases | 1.004× | 1.035× | 1.805× |
| Rotating weights, 55 cases | 1.003× | 1.016× | 1.409× |

The heuristic is already strong on these workloads; tuning adds about 1.6–3.5%. Refreshing the previous tuning adds only 0.3–0.4%. These are kernel graph timings; individual timing losses remain, and no new eager or model-throughput comparison is claimed.

Validation: **249 passed, 1 skipped, 1 unrelated INT8 checkpoint test deselected**; **286 loader/selector queries passed**; full changed-file pre-commit passed. Fresh TP1 servers loaded all six relevant tables and selected the native Triton backend. The same 64-question, five-shot, greedy GSM8K sanity sample scored previous 61/64 versus updated 62/64, with no invalid/API errors; this small sample does not establish an accuracy improvement.

<details>
<summary>Numerical observation retained from validation</summary>

One extra verification failed a Torch comparison at M/N/K=(64,4096,3840): one of 262,144 values differed by 0.017578125 at the unchanged heuristic entry. Ten isolated repeats per seed and implementation matched a full FP32 reference, and the complete annotated rerun passed at unchanged `rtol=atol=1e-2`. The isolated failure remains unexplained and is not claimed fixed.

</details>

Current tuning commands (omit `--save-path` for print-only results):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tp-size 1 --gpus 0 1 --save-path ./fp8-configs

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tp-size 2 --gpus 0 1 --save-path ./fp8-configs
```

### Earlier R9700 retuning (`dba246dd44`; historical)

In `dba246dd44`, retuned the 11 existing BF16-output N/K families on both R9700/gfx1201 GPUs at M=1,2,4,...,32768: 176 search points, with **103 tuned entries and 73 explicit heuristic fallbacks**. A measured entry applies only at its exact M; unmeasured token counts retain the production heuristic. Existing tables without the new flags preserve their previous nearest-M behavior. The tuner now compares the actual RDNA heuristic and exports a tuned entry only above its minimum gain (default 2% and 0.15 µs).

Independent measurements use the actual runtime backends, fresh inputs, shuffled paired rounds, and graph/eager timing after compilation. Across 352 anchor GPU-case records:

| Measurement | Speedup vs heuristic-only | Speedup vs Torch RowWise |
|---|---:|---:|
| Captured graph GPU time | 1.030× | 1.799× |
| Batched eager completion | 1.004× | 1.708× |
| CPU submission | 0.883× | 0.982× |

The selected tuned points alone average 1.051× graph speedup over the heuristic. Unmeasured-M and rotating-weight controls are retained, including adverse samples and followups. Host lookup adds about 13.2% CPU submission latency versus heuristic-only; these are primarily graph-serving optimizations.

Fresh Gemma 4 12B TP1 graph serving uses BF16, FP8 KV cache, AITER unified attention, AITER linear off, max sequences 8, max batched tokens 8192, max model length 32768, and 1/2/4/8 streams × eight turns × 2048 new prompt tokens/turn × 128 output tokens/request. Six primary servers start with separate empty compiler caches, using reverse backend order on GPU1; all 720 primary requests are included.

| Streams | Primary mean request output-rate change vs heuristic | Change vs Torch RowWise |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | −9.79% | +9.89% |
| 2 | −5.14% | +15.92% |
| 4 | −4.83% | +15.94% |
| 8 | −2.59% | +16.44% |

These percentages are geometric means of the two same-GPU pairs, not confidence intervals. The first GPU1 tuned server has an unresolved persistent decode slowdown. Two additional diagnostic servers add 240 successful requests: an all-heuristic table control closely matches heuristic-only, while a tuned repeat is −3.42% at one stream and +0.87–1.60% at 2–8 streams against its saved same-GPU heuristic baseline.

A post-hoc comparison excludes the first turn and the union of turn groups overlapping recorded Triton compilation writes, identically across all seven relevant runs (92 requests retained per run). GPU0's primary tuned run and GPU1's later tuned repeat are within 0.08% of heuristic-only at one stream and +0.87–1.59% at 2–8 streams. The original slow GPU1 run remains −13.39% to −6.85% versus heuristic after these exclusions. This is not a new fully prewarmed benchmark, and the favorable repeat does not replace the original primary result.

Numerical/backend validation on the tuning source: **232 passed, 1 unrelated INT8 checkpoint test deselected**; contributed CLI validation **77/77 passed**. Full-output Torch comparison, sampled FP32 checks, legacy lookup compatibility (97,647 queries), and exact/fallback routing (129 queries) passed. The same 64-question, five-shot, greedy GSM8K sanity sample gives Torch 63/64, heuristic 62/64, retuned 61/64, with no invalid answers; this small sample does not establish quality equivalence.

The performance and model-quality data above use `0435cb2d20` plus this retuning patch, before the subsequent upstream merge `8b4315147c`. After integrating that merge, the numerical/backend suite passed **249 tests, 1 skipped, 1 deselected**, the contributed CLI passed **77/77 validations**, and full changed-file pre-commit passed. The serving measurements are not relabeled as post-merge results. No custom FP8 startup warmup was restored, and enforced-eager model throughput was not rerun.

Historical validation command at `dba246dd44` (uses the former CLI; current tuning commands are above):

```bash
uv run benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
  --shapes 3840,2048 3840,4096 3840,7680 3840,8192 3840,15360 \
    4096,3840 5120,3840 8192,3840 9216,3840 15360,3840 30720,3840 \
  --m 1 2 8 33 128 2048 8192 --validate-only \
  --rounds 3 --rep-ms 3 --output-dir fp8-retune-validation
```

### Earlier untuned RDNA heuristic update (2026-10-29, before retuning)

The earlier heuristic update included the work through `0435cb2d20`. Backend eligibility does not require a tuning file. RDNA devices with FP8 support use the new heuristic; existing tuned maps take priority within their covered token-count ranges. Processor count and cache capacity are read during backend initialization, and selections/compiled launchers are cached. That earlier update did not change tuning JSON files; the retuning above replaces them. There is no custom FP8 startup warmup: ordinary graph preparation and first-use JIT compile the required variants.

| Evidence | Result and scope |
|---|---|
| Broad untuned comparison with Torch RowWise, initial heuristic study (`6a1dbbe971`) | 2,170-shape regression corpus: 1.93× graph / 1.76× batched-eager geometric speedup. Material-loss counts fell from 37 to 1 for graph and 34 to 1 for eager; followups across the broader study confirmed two graph-only shape losses. |
| Gemma 4 12B untuned graph serving, same initial study | TP1 on R9700, BF16, FP8 KV, AITER unified attention, AITER linear off; 1/2/4/8 streams, eight turns, 2,048 new prompt tokens and 128 output tokens/request. Two fresh matched repeats per arm/mode; 1,440 successful requests across Torch/old/new and graph/eager. Mean per-request output rate versus Torch improved 8.21–12.39% with graphs; this includes TTFT and first-use records. |
| Capacity generalization and consolidation | Reference R9700 choices preserved. Final consolidation matched 823,368 selector cases, 29,997 tile mappings, and all 144 paired runtime GPU instruction sections. Paired graph latency changed +0.09% untuned / −0.12% with tuning maps present; initial flags stayed below material graph/eager thresholds on nine-round followups. |
| Final runtime (`848373c3bd`), after warmup removal | 238 numerical/backend-selection tests passed, one unrelated INT8 checkpoint test deselected; pre-commit passed. Fresh untuned Gemma startup, graph capture, and two inference requests passed. This was a model smoke, not a new throughput or quality comparison. |
| Latest test-only cleanup (`0435cb2d20`) | 28 relevant kernel/generic-selection tests passed; pre-commit passed. Removed heuristic-policy/cache-discovery unit tests and retained numerical kernel coverage gated to RDNA with FP8 support. Production tree is identical to `848373c3bd`. |

**Limits:** The broad/Torch-serving results above predate capacity generalization and removal of custom warmup; they are not a fresh full-throughput run of the final tip. At reference hardware capacities the choices are preserved, and subsequent graph controls and final smoke provide narrower validation. Two repeated graph-only losses versus Torch remain at M/N/K=(65,18944,3584) and (65,19968,5632), with +14.7% and +3.9% graph latency. A later fresh-process eager model comparison during capacity generalization showed a 12.5–17.0% slowdown versus the prior heuristic and remains unresolved; graph production was prioritized. Performance measurements are from gfx1201, while other processor/cache profiles have simulated numerical/policy coverage. These results support the measured graph-serving workloads, not a guarantee of no regressions for every shape or architecture. Full model-quality evaluation has not been repeated for this heuristic update.

The accuracy and 512-output-token serving sections below are earlier validation with their existing provenance; the 128-output-token study above is separate.

Test environment: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / gfx1201, Torch 2.13 with ROCm 10, and Triton 3.8. Model: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic`.

Validation covers operator correctness, backend selection, compiled execution, graph replay, strided scales, and tile/layout boundaries. Kernel comparisons use identical FP8 operands and scales against Torch RowWise, with quantization excluded from the timings. Serving performance compares Torch RowWise and native Triton with the same attention backend and AITER linear disabled.

```bash
uv run pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_triton_scaled_mm.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py \
  -k 'not rocm_compressed_tensors_w8a8'
```

Earlier operator and backend-selection validation, before the heuristic update: **152 passed, 1 deselected** (INT8 checkpoint smoke test excluded by the command above). Pre-commit checks passed. The simplification removes launch-recording fixtures, exact tuning-policy assertions, and redundant large-shape cases while retaining numerical correctness, compiled dynamic shapes, graph replay with mutated inputs/scales, strided scales, and operand-boundary coverage. The shared Triton kernel and tuning configurations are unchanged from the benchmarked version. The fresh serving comparison below completed **480 successful requests**, with no errors or incomplete requests.

Historical benchmark correctness validation (using the former CLI below) uses `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=atol=1e-2`. **44 cases** (11 installed shapes × M=1/64/256/2048) passed for both heuristic and tuned paths. BF16/FP16 smoke checks passed, and injected mismatches and non-finite outputs were rejected.

```bash
uv run benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
  --shapes 3840,2048 3840,4096 3840,7680 3840,8192 3840,15360 \
    4096,3840 5120,3840 8192,3840 9216,3840 15360,3840 30720,3840 \
  --m 1 64 256 2048 --validate-only --rep-ms 1 --rounds 1 \
  --output-dir fp8-validation
```

### Accuracy validation

GSM8K accuracy was evaluated with vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` on the full **1,319-question** test set: **5-shot**, greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, seed 42), chat completions with thinking disabled, a 1,024-token output limit, and 32 concurrent requests. Both runs used **TP2**, **FP8 KV cache**, and default serving settings, changing only `--linear-backend`. Attention was selected automatically (`TRITON_ATTN`); no attention or AITER environment override was used. Evaluated PR commit: `bf64ce9836f2`.

| Backend | Correct / questions | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Torch RowWise | 1,255 / 1,319 | 95.15% | 0 |
| Native Triton | 1,251 / 1,319 | 94.84% | 0 |

Triton minus Torch RowWise: **-0.30 percentage points**. In the paired comparison, Triton answered 13 questions correctly that Torch missed, and missed 17 questions Torch answered correctly. Triton answered 4 fewer questions correctly in this single run. All **2,638 evaluation requests** completed successfully; 0 responses reached the output-token limit. These results cover this model and GSM8K configuration; other models and platforms need separate evaluation.

This accuracy comparison uses default attention. The TP1 serving performance measurements below use explicitly selected `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`.

To reproduce, start each server separately, using `torch` for the baseline and `triton` for the candidate:

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --linear-backend torch
```

Run the evaluator against each server:

```bash
uv run tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --use-chat-completions \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42 \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 \
  --request-timeout-seconds 7200 \
  --save-results gsm8k-results.json
```

### Serving commands

Install vLLM from this PR. Run each configuration separately on the same GPU.

**TP1 baseline (Torch RowWise)**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --linear-backend torch
```

**TP1 native Triton**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --linear-backend triton
```

### Workload

Benchmark with GuideLLM 0.7.3:

- 8 turns.
- 2048 configured prompt tokens per turn.
- 512 output tokens per request.
- 1/2/4/8 streams with 8/16/32/64 requests.

### Results

<!-- native-triton-serving-results:start -->
End-to-end TP1 serving: Torch RowWise versus native Triton, using the commands above. Two fresh-server runs per backend use reversed order. Each baseline/candidate pair stays on the same GPU, with empty compilation caches for each server. All four profiles reach their configured concurrency and preserve all eight turns.

Each cell shows **Torch RowWise → native Triton (percentage change)**. Output tok/s is the mean per-request output rate (output tokens divided by end-to-end request latency). Absolute measurements are kept separate for the two same-GPU pairs. The summary percentages below are geometric means of their Triton/RowWise ratios. Every successful request, including warmup/cooldown and first-use requests, is included. Positive output-rate changes and negative TTFT/E2E changes improve performance.

| Pair | Streams | Mean output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 28.09 → 32.62 (**+16.1%**) | 915 → 1,153 (+26.0%) | 18.24 → 15.74 (**−13.7%**) |
| 1 | 2 | 26.82 → 31.41 (**+17.1%**) | 1,149 → 1,139 (**−0.9%**) | 19.10 → 16.32 (**−14.6%**) |
| 1 | 4 | 24.79 → 28.80 (**+16.1%**) | 1,850 → 1,800 (**−2.7%**) | 20.70 → 17.84 (**−13.8%**) |
| 1 | 8 | 20.88 → 23.91 (**+14.5%**) | 2,911 → 2,823 (**−3.0%**) | 24.65 → 21.56 (**−12.5%**) |
| 2 | 1 | 28.09 → 32.70 (**+16.4%**) | 925 → 1,135 (+22.7%) | 18.24 → 15.71 (**−13.9%**) |
| 2 | 2 | 26.64 → 31.38 (**+17.8%**) | 1,171 → 1,123 (**−4.1%**) | 19.23 → 16.33 (**−15.1%**) |
| 2 | 4 | 24.57 → 28.59 (**+16.4%**) | 1,776 → 1,673 (**−5.8%**) | 20.88 → 17.97 (**−13.9%**) |
| 2 | 8 | 20.65 → 23.60 (**+14.3%**) | 3,011 → 2,872 (**−4.6%**) | 24.93 → 21.88 (**−12.2%**) |

Mean per-request output rate improves by **14.4–17.4%** across the four stream levels. Mean request latency falls by **12.4–14.8%**. Mean TTFT increases at 1 stream (**+24.4%**). First-use requests remain included in the measurements.

These are synthetic-text serving measurements. GSM8K accuracy is evaluated separately above at TP2 with default attention. Multimodal inputs and performance on other architectures remain to be validated.

[Full comparison, per-turn charts, raw results, and provenance](https://github.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm-bench-collection/blob/4f92502e7036abbcc535daac8dda4147fe41b8ec/comparisons/gfx1201/gemma-4-12b-fp8-dynamic/rocm10-native-triton-pr61091-tp1-20261012-v1/README.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,515 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tune native per-token FP8 GEMM with transposed weights and BF16 output.
+
+Example:
+    uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python \
+        benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
+        --model MODEL_ID --tp-size 1 --gpus 0 1 \
+        --save-path ./fp8-configs
+
+The default search sweeps powers-of-two M from 1 through 32768, refines the
+best tiles, and confirms winners against the production RDNA heuristic in
+seven paired rounds. Model IDs select matrix workloads from weight_shapes.py;
+model configuration and weights are not loaded. Expert kernels are separate.
+Omit --save-path to print results without exporting tuning files.
+
+"""
+
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+import multiprocessing as mp
+import os
+import random
+import statistics
+import time
+from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+from weight_shapes import TP_WEIGHT_SHAPES, WEIGHT_SHAPES
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils import (
+    fp8_per_token_heuristic as heuristic,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
+    get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config_filename,
+    get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_configs,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import get_device_name_as_file_name, num_compute_units
+
+BATCH_SIZES = tuple(2**i for i in range(16))
+
+
+def get_weight_shapes(model, tp_size):
+    """Read (N, K) GEMM dimensions from the shared shape catalog."""
+    if tp_size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("TP size must be positive")
+    if model in TP_WEIGHT_SHAPES:
+        if tp_size not in TP_WEIGHT_SHAPES[model]:
+            raise ValueError(f"No matrix shapes recorded for {model} at TP={tp_size}")
+        return sorted({(n, k) for k, n in TP_WEIGHT_SHAPES[model][tp_size]})
+    if model not in WEIGHT_SHAPES:
+        raise ValueError(f"Add {model}'s matrix shapes to weight_shapes.py first")
+    shapes = set()
+    for dimensions, split_dim in WEIGHT_SHAPES[model]:
+        dimensions = list(dimensions)
+        if dimensions[split_dim] % tp_size:
+            raise ValueError("TP size must divide the matrix's partitioned dimension")
+        dimensions[split_dim] //= tp_size
+        k, n = dimensions
+        shapes.add((n, k))
+    return sorted(shapes)
+
+
+def launch_config(config):
+    return {
+        "engine": "shared",
+        "block_size_m": config["BLOCK_SIZE_M"],
+        "block_size_n": config["BLOCK_SIZE_N"],
+        "block_size_k": config["BLOCK_SIZE_K"],
+        "num_warps": config["num_warps"],
+        "num_stages": config["num_stages"],
+        "group_m": config.get("GROUP_M", 1),
+        "n_stripe": config.get("N_STRIPE", 0),
+        "unmasked_loads": bool(config.get("UNMASKED_LOADS", False)),
+    }
+
+
+def staged_candidates(heuristic, previous):
+    keys = ("BLOCK_SIZE_M", "BLOCK_SIZE_N", "BLOCK_SIZE_K", "num_warps", "num_stages")
+    choices = [
+        launch_config(dict(zip(keys, values)))
+        for values in itertools.product(
+            (16, 32, 64, 128), (32, 64, 128), (64, 128, 256), (4, 8), (1, 2, 3)
+        )
+    ]
+    for bm, bn, bk in [(128, 256, 64), (128, 256, 128), (256, 64, 64), (256, 128, 64)]:
+        for warps, stages in [(4, 1), (4, 2), (8, 1), (8, 2)]:
+            choices.append(
+                launch_config(
+                    dict(
+                        BLOCK_SIZE_M=bm,
+                        BLOCK_SIZE_N=bn,
+                        BLOCK_SIZE_K=bk,
+                        num_warps=warps,
+                        num_stages=stages,
+                    )
+                )
+            )
+    if previous is not None:
+        choices.append(previous)
+    if heuristic is not None:
+        choices.append(
+            launch_config(
+                dict(
+                    BLOCK_SIZE_M=heuristic["block_size_m"],
+                    BLOCK_SIZE_N=heuristic["block_size_n"],
+                    BLOCK_SIZE_K=heuristic["block_size_k"],
+                    num_warps=heuristic.get("num_warps", 4),
+                    num_stages=heuristic.get("num_stages", 2),
+                )
+            )
+        )
+    return choices
+
+
+def staged_refinements(ranked, m, n, k):
+    choices = []
+    for row in ranked[:4]:
+        config = row["config"]

+## Native Triton per-token FP8 on ROCm
+
+On ROCm GPUs with native FP8 support, `--linear-backend triton` selects the
+native Triton backend for dynamic per-token activation scales and per-channel
+weight scales. It supports BF16 and FP16 output. With the default
+`--linear-backend auto`, this backend is considered after higher-priority
+compatible ROCm backends and before Torch RowWise.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
+  --language-model-only --max-model-len 32768 \
+  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --linear-backend triton
+```
+
+Tuning files are optional. FP8-capable RDNA GPUs use a hardware-aware launch
+heuristic when no tuned configuration applies. The Radeon AI PRO R9700 BF16
+tuning tables apply measured configurations only at their exact token counts;
+intermediate counts and entries without a reliable measured gain retain the
+heuristic. Here, token count means the rows processed by the current linear
+operation, including any graph padding, rather than the full context length.
+
+### Reproducing per-token FP8 tuning
+
+`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py` tunes per-token FP8 GEMMs
+with BF16 output on FP8-capable RDNA GPUs. Select a model workload from
+`benchmarks/kernels/weight_shapes.py`, its tensor-parallel size, and the GPUs
+to use as parallel tuning workers. The script uses matrix dimensions and TP
+split information only; model configuration and weights are not loaded.
+Expert kernels are separate.
+
+```bash
+uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python \
+  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
+  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
+  --tp-size 1 --gpus 0 1 --save-path ./fp8-configs
+```

+`--tp-size` (alias `-tp`) describes the model's tensor parallelism and defaults
+to 1. It is independent of the number of tuning workers. Standard catalog entries
+divide the recorded TP axis; layouts requiring other partitioning use explicit
+per-TP matrix shapes from `TP_WEIGHT_SHAPES`.
+`--gpus` defaults to all visible GPUs; selected GPUs must be the same model.
+
+To cover TP2 as well, run the same command with `--tp-size 2`:

+  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
+  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \

+configurations and the heuristic tile, refinement of the best four choices,

+than 2% and 0.15 microseconds and win at least five rounds. Selected results pass

The shared `triton_scaled_mm` changes do affect existing INT8 callers, so I checked end-to-end Quark INT8 inference against the original shared implementation.

The Quark INT8 route is `QuarkW8A8Int8.apply_weights` → `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` → INT8 activation quantization → `triton_scaled_mm` → `scaled_mm_kernel`. It retains the default launch policy and skips `_get_scaled_mm_launch_policy`; the new FP8 tuning-config loader is not on this route. `_scaled_mm_tile_coords` runs as compiled Triton.

I ran [Gemma 4 12B Quark W8A8 INT8](https://huggingface.co/rajasingh012/gemma-4-12b-it-quark-w8a8-int8) on two AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs (gfx1201) with TP2, default cuda graph mode.  Both cases explicitly select the existing Triton INT8 backend. 

The run was testing using the same benchmark configs in the Pr Message above.

| Streams | Per-request output TPS change | Mean TTFT change | Mean end-to-end latency change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +0.15% | −4.70% | −0.29% |
| 2 | +0.67% | −10.06% | −0.93% |
| 4 | +0.63% | −8.72% | −1.22% |
| 8 | −1.63% | +4.86% | +2.50% |

Positive TPS changes and negative latency changes improve performance. Runtime logs confirm over 16,000 FULL graph replays in each case. Replay bypasses repeated Python wrapper/launch work inside captured regions; uncaptured prefill and other serving overhead remain.

The measured serving impact is small in this graph-enabled Quark test, with no consistent slowdown across stream levels.

For the CUDA CUTLASS path, I also inspected checkpoint/config coverage. When CUTLASS is selected, the shared wrapper uses native CUTLASS if the weight's K and N dimensions are multiples of 16. The FP8 CUTLASS linear backend also pads weights and activations to satisfy this alignment. Grouping the inspected checkpoints by architecture, size, and precision gives three distinct examples:

| Model group (representative checkpoint) | Evidence for avoiding the shared Triton fallback |
|---|---|
| [Gemma 4 12B FP8 Dynamic](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic) | Local checkpoint inspection: all 328 FP8 matrices have aligned K/N dimensions. |
| [Qwen2.5-VL 3B W8A8 INT8](https://huggingface.co/lsm0729/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8) | Published configs: quantized text-layer dimensions are aligned; vision layers are excluded from INT8. Groups the inspected 3B W8A8 and SmoothQuant variants. |
